claims.text: The model has one precondition: the founder already has an app with traction, paying customers, profit and growth, and more than one investor wants in.
claims.quote: This model has one precondition, and it matters. The founder has an app with traction: paying customers, profit, growth.

claims.text: With generative AI that position is no longer rare, because agents make execution cheap enough for a founder who knows the problem to reach profit before raising anything.
claims.quote: agents make execution cheap enough that a founder who knows the problem can build, sell and reach profit before raising anything.

claims.text: Sell, don't issue: the investor buys shares the founder already owns in a private sale, the money goes to the founder, and the company is not diluted.
claims.quote: In this model, the investor buys shares the founder already owns, in a private sale. The money goes to the founder.

claims.text: In the UK, with Business Asset Disposal Relief, the first £1 million of lifetime qualifying gains is taxed at 18% from 6 April 2026, and gains above at 24%.
claims.quote: the first £1 million of lifetime qualifying gains is taxed at 18% from 6 April 2026

value.unit: percent tax on the first £1 million of qualifying gains

claims.text: A secondary sale does not by itself require preferred shares, board seats, vetoes or liquidation preferences; the investor buys the vision, not the steering wheel.
claims.quote: A secondary sale does not, by itself, require preferred shares, board seats, vetoes or liquidation preferences.

claims.text: Kaplan and Strömberg found that when a company performs very well, the VCs retain their cash-flow rights but relinquish most of their control and liquidation rights; this model starts there.
claims.quote: the VCs retain their cash-flow rights, but relinquish most of their control and liquidation rights

claims.text: Lend, don't dilute: if the company needs money, the founder lends some of the proceeds back, subordinated to every other creditor, repaid if the company succeeds, at a modest fixed rate or none.
claims.quote: the founder puts some of the sale proceeds back in, as a loan. The terms are simple: subordinated to every other creditor, repaid if the company succeeds

claims.text: A loan from the founder carries no board seat and no veto, so nobody outside gains control in exchange for the money.
claims.quote: a loan from the founder carries no board seat and no veto.

claims.text: Open source protects the investor too: if investors lose faith in the founder's direction, they can take the code and fund a different team to build a better service on it.
claims.quote: Open source protects the investor too. If the investors lose faith in the founder's direction, they do not need control of the company to act on it

claims.text: A competitor who forks the code today gets the position as of today, not the velocity; customers stay for the service, the quality and the trust.
claims.quote: A competitor who forks our code today gets our position as of today. They do not get our velocity.

claims.text: The owner's estimate is that an established company of a few hundred people with a full copy of the code needs three months at best and closer to a year to reach where the original team is.
claims.quote: needs three months at best and closer to a year realistically to reach where the original team already is.

value.unit: months at best for a fork to catch up, closer to a year realistically

claims.text: The fork disciplines the founder because it is possible and protects the founder because it is slow, so neither side has a stick big enough to bully the other.
claims.quote: the fork disciplines the founder because it is possible, and protects the founder because it is slow.

claims.text: The licence must be genuinely open, and the copyright structure matters more than the licence file: every catalogued relicensing between 2018 and 2024 was by a single corporate copyright holder.
claims.quote: every catalogued relicensing between 2018 and 2024 was made by a single corporate copyright holder that had gathered contributors' copyright.

claims.text: In the worked example, a £2 million sale of 20% of a £10 million UK company costs the founder about £420,000 in tax and leaves about £1.58 million to decide with.
claims.quote: the founder pays about £420,000 in tax (18% on the first £1 million and 24% on the second), and has about £1.58 million to decide with

value.unit: GBP tax on a £2 million sale in the worked example

claims.text: The structure does not just suit the founder; it raises the chance that the company succeeds, through money discipline, focus and direction.
claims.quote: this structure does not just suit the founder; it raises the chance that the company succeeds.

claims.text: The Startup Genome study of more than 3,200 startups found 74% of high growth internet startups fail due to premature scaling.
claims.quote: 74% of high growth internet startups fail due to premature scaling

value.unit: percent of high growth internet startups failing from premature scaling

claims.text: A founder who has taken some chips off the table can rationally swing for a large outcome, and is not tempted by the first acquisition offer.
claims.quote: can rationally swing for a large outcome

claims.text: EIS gives UK investors 30% income tax relief and SEIS 50%, but only on shares that are newly issued and paid for in full, so bought shares carry no relief.
claims.quote: EIS gives investors 30% income tax relief and SEIS 50%, but only on shares that are "newly issued and paid for in full"

value.unit: percent income tax relief under EIS, lost on bought shares

claims.text: One industry guide puts discounts for common stock at 10% to 30% to the last primary round, while an EY analysis of 306 Indian deals found 85% priced in line with it.
claims.quote: an EY analysis of 306 Indian deals found 85% priced in line with the primary round.

value.unit: percent of Indian secondary deals priced in line with the primary round

claims.text: Balderton has walked away from high quality businesses over the size of the secondary asked for, and would not expect a founder to sell more than 10% of their holding at the growth stage.
claims.quote: As a good rule of thumb, we would not expect a founder to sell more than 10% of their overall holding at the growth stage.

claims.text: A founder who sells shares and lends back the proceeds has moved part of their risk ahead of the investors who just bought in, because a loan normally ranks ahead of shares.
claims.quote: a founder who sells shares and lends back the proceeds has moved part of their risk ahead of the investors who just bought in.

claims.text: In Germany shareholder loans are subordinated to all other creditors in insolvency and repayments within a year before filing can be clawed back; the UK has no automatic rule.
claims.quote: shareholder loans are subordinated to all other creditors in insolvency, and repayments made within a year before filing can be clawed back.

claims.text: The honest version writes the subordination in: the founder's loan ranks behind every other creditor by contract and is repaid only from success.
claims.quote: the founder's loan is subordinated by contract, ranking behind every other creditor, and repaid only from success.

claims.text: For a director, shares are employment-related securities, and HMRC can charge the excess over market value as employment income rather than a capital gain.
claims.quote: HMRC can charge the excess over market value as employment income rather than a capital gain.

claims.text: Refuse a broad non-compete, which keeps the fork for the investors and takes it from the founder, and offer narrow protections: confidentiality, no poaching, no use of the brand.
claims.quote: Refuse it, and offer narrow protections instead: confidentiality, no poaching of staff or customers for a period, and no use of the brand.

claims.text: In the UK the 2023 plan to cap non-competes at three months was never legislated, and a new consultation closed in February 2026 without a decision.
claims.quote: the 2023 plan to cap non-competes at three months was never legislated, and a new consultation closed in February 2026 without a decision

claims.text: The fork protects the thesis, not the stake: investors who fork and fund a rival are competing with their own investment.
claims.quote: The fork protects the thesis, not the stake.

claims.text: A hybrid keeps most of the benefit: a modest tranche of new ordinary shares that qualify for EIS, a smaller slice of the founder's shares, and a subordinated founder loan for any shortfall.
claims.quote: issue a modest tranche of new ordinary shares that can qualify for EIS, then sell a smaller slice of the founder's shares, and make up any shortfall with a subordinated founder loan.

claims.text: This is the best case for the founder; it assumes leverage most founders do not have.
claims.quote: This is the best case for the founder. It assumes leverage most founders do not have.

claims.text: No study tests this model; the claim that it raises the odds is an argument from discipline and incentives, not data.
claims.quote: No study tests this model. The claim that it raises the odds is an argument from discipline and incentives, not data.

claims.text: The fork as insurance is an argument, not a tested mechanism; it depends on the code being genuinely open and investors being able to fund a credible alternative.
claims.quote: The fork as insurance is an argument, not a tested mechanism.

claims.text: This is not tax or legal advice: the UK figures are for 2026/27, BADR has conditions, and other countries differ.
claims.quote: Not tax or legal advice. The UK figures are for 2026/27, BADR has conditions, and other countries differ.

claims.text: The worked example is illustrative; real valuations, base costs and tax positions will change the numbers.
claims.quote: The worked example is illustrative. Real valuations, base costs and tax positions will change the numbers.

claims.text: The secondary pricing data is thin: the EY figures are Indian deals and the discount range is from one industry guide; and investors are not the enemy.
claims.quote: The secondary pricing data is thin. The EY figures are Indian deals; the discount range is from one industry guide.

claims.text: The owner has a stake: he is a founder, his companies run on open source, and this model suits him.
claims.quote: I have a stake. I am a founder, my companies run on open source, and this model suits me.
